set.approach: The wall is reached from the Miette Hot Springs road, which leaves Highway 16 northeast of Jasper; the viewpoint on that road shows the wall and the line of the approach. Park in the small pullout on the left a short drive beyond the viewpoint. Walk toward the creek, turn left on the trail down along it, and cross it (a fixed rope helps when the water is up). Then follow the steep trail marked with orange tape up to the base of the ridge; the last stretch is through a few cliff bands with some scrambling and bushwhacking. The route starts on a good ledge beside a small pine, a good way right of Good Intentions Bad Habits.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the ridge above, and the way down is to walk off along the ridge. Rappelling the route is possible with a long rope, though loose rock lies on parts of it; an emergency rappel station sits low on the first pitch.

set.approach: Take the good trail from the Ashlar parking lot to the last hump below the ridge. There, traverse left beneath the wall to the scree, climb the faint switchbacks to a point just above the start of the route, and traverse the scree back to the wall. The first pitch starts from a little ledge beside the shallow crack that slants left up the face, on its right. The parking is the small pullout past the viewpoint on the Miette Hot Springs road; from it the trail goes down to the creek, crosses it and climbs the steep hill to the ridge.
set.descent_text: The route tops out on the ridge, and the way down is to walk off along the ridge.

set.approach: The crag is reached from the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper: turn onto Highway 93A at Athabasca Falls, drive past the falls to Leech Lake, and park in the pullout there or in the small one a little further on, on the left. A well-kept trail leads into the forest to the crag. Walk along the base of the cliff past the first couple of short bolted lines until the routes become clean and taller, with big rocks on the ground below. Bourgeois follows the weakness to a small roof in this first taller sector.

set.approach: Start on the Castle Mountain fire lookout trail, which leaves Highway 1A west of Castle Junction. From the lookout, a trail heads north and up, getting steeper, to a gully; cross it to the east and pick the trail up again. It continues steeply to the bottom of the trail that serves Castle Mountain Hut, where rappel bolts are visible at the top. From there head climbers' left (west) to a bowl-shaped wall; the bolts of the first pitch are easy to spot.
set.descent_text: Walking off is the most direct way down: from the top on the plateau head east toward the Castle Mountain Hut access trail, which has a few short fourth class downclimbing sections and an optional rappel, then retrace the approach to the fire lookout. The route can also be rappelled with a long rope; the first rappel from the top ends at a station partway down the face, off to the side of the last pitch's bolts, and skipping it will stick the ropes. The belay anchors are all fixed.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts; descent stated on the route page or its own crag page.

set.approach: Take the Rockbound Lake trail from its trailhead just east of Castle Junction on Highway 1A, as far as the turnoff for the Lost Lemon crag. Continue a short way beyond it, then head up and left through forest to a drainage. At the wall the prow of The Moat is obvious; the route starts at its toe, on the lower tier beneath Castles in the Sky.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the ledge below Castles in the Sky. From there either continue up that route, or traverse the ledge to the right back to the Eisenhower Tower trail: the traverse is a hike on steep ground above the lower cliff band, with bolts along the first stretch for those who want to stay roped, and easier-angled ground after that. Keep high until you can curl around to the base of the first Eisenhower tier on its east side, where the trail starts and leads out.

set.approach: Park in the roadside pullout with a garbage bin on Highway 16 east of Jasper, just past the bridge, and take the main hiking trail that starts behind the lot. The crag soon appears ahead. Where the trail forks faintly below a rolling rise, go right, then work up switchbacks and over a meadow to the wall. Cinquefoil Center is right of a thick tree at the foot of the crag, and the approach trail leads straight to it. Art of Madness climbs right of the main roof, in the middle of Cinquefoil Center.
